title: Ringed geometric coefficient presentations before realization
statement: For a prime $\ell$ and finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], take the completed ring sheaf $B_W$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and its positive constant quotients $A_{n,W}$. A coefficient family is a ring sheaf $R_W$ on each scheme with specified inverse-image identifications; a change is a compatible family of ring maps. Completed and finite families have their canonical coefficient pullbacks and projections. The ringed image attached to a chosen factorization $f=pj$ is the exact derived open extension followed by ordinary derived proper image, $P_R=Rp_*j_!$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Scalar extension is actual derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The open restriction square is determined by the open adjunction units [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact, lem-cbc-ringed-open-scalar-adjunction]; its inverse followed by proper restriction gives the compact-support restriction square. Its scalar-adjunction transpose is comparison. The completed pullback isomorphisms come from inverse image of the profinite coefficient limit, normalized on every finite quotient [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. These constructions contain no constructible realization or assertion that a scalar comparison is invertible.

proof.text: These are existing concrete constructions: exact open extension and ordinary right derived image give image. Ring change adjunctions transpose the restriction square to comparison. Open scalar restriction preserves the essential image of slice extension, so the specified open restriction mate is invertible. The completed coefficient pullback is determined by its finite constant projections; inverse image of the profinite coefficient limit gives its inverse, and equality on projections gives composition. This node isolates these declarations from the later realization theorems that share their broad former owner.
